races.name: Seamus Byrne Electrical Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Anyway
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid similar-going record (2W3P in Good conditions) and strong course experience; David Budds runner returns after 105 days off which is a stamina concern at 2m6f, but prominent style means it avoids the traffic problems that beset the rear-of-field brigade and it is ideally positioned to press Rocky's Diamond throughout.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field, trained by Declan Queally who is in strong 4/10 form over 14 days; the 6-day turnaround is a slight flag but this horse won last time out over 25f on Good ground and its ability to control tempo uncontested is the defining tactical fact of the race — Michael Kenneally (5lb claimer) adds a weight advantage.

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a strong recent profile including a win and a second over shorter Good ground trips; trained by Gavin Cromwell (2/23 in 14 days suggests modest yard form) and wears a hood, which may sharpen its jumping — proven at 20f, stepping up to 2m6f is the key question for this closer at Tramore.

runners_data.name: More Coko
runners_data.note: A Willie Mullins-trained hold-up horse returning after 131 days off, carrying the highest trainer 14-day strike rate in the field (14/47) but its own form string of 92F66 on its recent starts is uninspiring; best form figures came over 17f on Good and it steps up sharply in trip today, making stamina its primary concern over 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Joe
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose tendency to fade in the finish is already flagged; bumped to midfield on the pace map due to the volume of hold-up types in this small field, it is in effect racing out of its natural position — trainer Walsh has 0/1 in the 14-day window and the 10-day turnaround following a run of poor form figures makes it hard to build a strong case here.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Diamond is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the front over this 2m6f trip on Good ground at Tramore, setting a sustainable and controlled pace without any natural rival to pressure or challenge for the lead. Anyway, as a prominent runner, will likely track closely in second, while the hold-up contingent of Thecompanysergeant, More Coko, and Rodeo Joe will race further back — though Rodeo Joe, a genuine hold-up type, has been mapped to midfield due to the field's composition rather than reflecting its true natural position. With Rocky's Diamond able to control tempo uncontested, this race shape classically favours horses with the stamina and class to close from off the pace on a true surface, but the single pace-setter scenario — particularly over this staying trip — also gives real hope to a prominent horse like Anyway who can sit just behind and pounce. The race shape most strongly favours hold-up and prominent types who have the class and jumping ability to pick off a potentially slowing front-runner in the latter stages, provided they have the stamina to sustain a run from 3 out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rocky's Diamond Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond sets a sustainable gallop and none of the closers can mount an effective run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond dictates every yard, the hold-up horses cover too much ground too late, and the even Good ground rewards a horse who has jumped and travelled fluently throughout; a prominent racer sitting close enough to capitalise benefits enormously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond's recent 6-day turnaround tells in the closing stages and the hold-up horses find a clear run.
scenarios.body: Thecompanysergeant, proven at this level with a recent course win over similar Good ground, is best placed to peg back a tiring leader from the final fence; More Coko's class for Mullins gives it an each-way profile if the pace collapses late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the race develops into a test of jumping fluency and stamina from the front group.
scenarios.body: Anyway, tracking closely in a prominent position, is drawn into a battle of attrition rather than a sprint finish and its experience over Good ground suits; its form figures of 2W3P in similar conditions give it legitimate each-way claims in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart with faller or dramatic errors and Rodeo Joe or More Coko benefit from chaos.
scenarios.body: Rodeo Joe, though a genuine hold-up type running partially out of role and flagged as fading in finishes, could benefit only from a truly chaotic sequence of events; More Coko remains the more plausible of these two to steal a reduced scenario.

watchPoints.text: Rocky's Diamond (front-runner, 6-day turnaround) — watch for signs of fatigue jumping the final two fences; if it weakens there, Thecompanysergeant and Anyway are the immediate dangers to capitalise.
More Coko returns after 131 days off and steps up significantly in trip — if it is less than fully wound up by Mullins, it may not see out the 2m6f on this Good ground and could fade from 3 out.

Rodeo Joe is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and is racing partially out of its natural role today — monitor its jumping fluency from halfway, as a series of jumping errors would confirm it is unlikely to threaten the principals late.

Anyway has had a 105-day break and its stamina at 2m6f returning from that layoff is unproven — if it struggles to maintain its prominent pitch turning for home, the race could open up for the closers behind.

races.name: I.P.R.S. Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Menas Miracle
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong sim-going record of 11 from 13 encounters on Good turf, two wins and four places; steps up to 2m6f having placed over 2m4f and 2m6f, and the 45-day break is not a concern given no obvious fitness flag from trainer Walsh's yard.

runners_data.name: Mercurial Sea
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent type with back-to-back placed runs at this level; trainer Slevin's yard is 1 from 2 in the last 14 days which is a minor positive, but the horse has yet to win and its form at 2m6f Good is untested.

runners_data.name: Pirate Island
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator who has struggled for form — six runs without a place finish in the historical record — and the quick 11-day turnaround after finishing ninth is a concern; tongue-strap fitted but little to recommend at this trip from a positional standpoint.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Hanlon's busy yard — 0 from 21 in the last 14 days is a stark trainer stat — placed twice on Good but a fence faller in recent form and hasn't threatened a win; the 7lb claim from Sexton is a partial mitigant.

runners_data.name: Our Zebo
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type returning from a lengthy 329-day break, which is the dominant concern; has won and placed multiple times on Good ground over 2m2f-3m, and Torrens knows the horse, but ring-rustiness in a big field over fences is a significant risk.

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four placed runs including a recent second over 2m5f Good; the five-year-old is progressive and travels well in this company, and trainer O'Brien fires with 1 from 5 in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; has placed third and won on Good ground over shorter and will control the fractions unchallenged; the absence of a pacemaking rival is the critical tactical advantage this horse holds regardless of its modest OR of 85.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Won last time on Good ground over 2m2f for Lanigan but has three consecutive pulled-ups before that; Slevin in the saddle is a positive and the horse clearly bounced back in the latest, but the erratic history over fences warrants caution in a 17-runner field.

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up type who will race more prominently than ideal given the field's composition; ran just six days ago and the quick turnaround on top of a going record of 14 from 15 on Good without a win makes the chance difficult to endorse, racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who fades in finishes and whose natural hold-up style will be compromised in this field; five days since last run, no win in recent form, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 underlines that it is unlikely to produce its best from a position closer to the pace than it prefers.

runners_data.name: Amburana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer at OR 76 with no wins on Good or Soft across five recent runs; placed third in a 2m2f Good race in the history and has shown brief promise but appears outclassed at the top of this handicap and has no headgear angle.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: A 13-year-old true hold-up type with a genuinely excellent placed record — five from five in the recent history including a win on Good — but finding itself raced closer than natural in this shape; form reads as the most talented of the redistributed hold-up group, and if this caveat is ignored by the market it could be an interesting each-way angle.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Five-year-old natural hold-up operator who has won and placed multiple times on Good at this trip; raced just seven days ago and while the form figures include a second and a win at 2m4f Good, it will be racing out of its preferred position — the STYLE_FIT flag is the chief caveat.

runners_data.name: Robin Elite
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes and has a poor recent record — three pulls-up in five, no place in the visible form — and will be racing closer than its natural hold-up tendency dictates; tongue-strap and the STYLE_FIT discount combine to make this a difficult proposition to support.

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for McCarthy's yard, which is 2 from 10 in the last 14 days; placed second on Good over 2m3f and has a win on Good in the history, but has no jockey listed which is a potential concern and is operating at OR 87 in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old true hold-up operator with a perfect sim-going record of 15 from 15 on Good, including a win; however it is racing out of its natural rear position in this field and finished eighth last time, with no jockey listed adding uncertainty — the historical going figures are enticing but the redistribution tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type at OR 95 who has placed on Good and Soft but pulled up last time; no jockey listed, 23-day break, and while the trip and going are familiar, the current form and positional challenge in a big field make it hard to make a strong case.

races.paceDynamic: Dunany Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure from another dedicated lead horse — meaning Kieren Buckley can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop through the early stages of this 2m6f trip on Good turf at Tramore. With only prominent types like Menas Miracle, Mercurial Sea, Thewaybackhome and My Cullen likely to push forward and track, the race shape will be orderly rather than frenetic, with Dunany Point landing in front and the prominent group settling just off the pace before the decisive fences in the home straight. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than can realistically race from the rear in a 17-runner field — Corkbeg, Bob The Builder, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Set The Tone, Robin Elite and U Asking Me are all genuine hold-up operators who are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural position, meaning the true back markers may be Shantou Show, Pirate Island and Tropical Image. This race shape — a controlled gallop set by one unchallenged front-runner — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace economically and pick it up from the front of the chasing pack, rather than true closers who will need a strong pace to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point is allowed to bowl along at a measured clip and the prominent pack tracks without disrupting the tempo.
scenarios.body: Buckley dictates a comfortable gallop, the race unfolds in slow motion until the last three fences, and horses that have settled just off the lead and conserved energy pounce from a position already close to the winner. Prominent racers who have tracked efficiently — Menas Miracle, Thewaybackhome, Mercurial Sea — are best placed to strike as the leader is challenged on the run to the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Surges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack collectively pushes Dunany Point harder than expected through the middle mile, creating just enough pace to stretch the field.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop develops as multiple horses press forward, tiring the front-runner in the final half-mile and opening the door for a prominent racer who travelled sweetly to assert from the second-last. Thewaybackhome's consistent placing form in this grade and Menas Miracle's good-ground figures make them the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough and the field spreads out enough to allow a true closer to pick off tired rivals late.
scenarios.body: This depends on horses redistributed to midfield — Corkbeg, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Set The Tone — actually finding themselves further back than shown, and the pace lifting enough to create a slog; given the one-pace-setter dynamic, that outcome is less probable. Fr Gilligansvoyge's consistent placed form in good ground over this trip gives it the best credentials among the hold-up brigade should this shape materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Jumping Reshuffles Race
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors scatter the field and multiple faller/unseater incidents break the established order.
scenarios.body: Falls or errors at the early fences in a 17-runner field could disrupt the front rank dramatically, bunching the field and turning the race into a stamina slog from halfway. Our Zebo, returning from 329 days off but with sound form at this trip and going, and Shantou Show, a hold-up type suited to a muddling test, would be the unlikely beneficiaries of a scrambled, attrition-based contest.

watchPoints.text: Dunany Point goes unchallenged to the front — watch whether any prominent runner (Menas Miracle, Thewaybackhome) pushes forward before the first fence to test the pace, as Buckley's ability to dictate entirely will define whether this turns into a true test or a sprint for home.

Our Zebo returns from 329 days off in a 17-runner chase over fences — any sign of ring-rustiness in the early jumping phases could cause significant interference for horses around it, particularly the prominent pack tracking the leader.

With six or more redistributed hold-up types forced to race in midfield, the early mid-race positioning battle between Corkbeg, Bob The Builder, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Set The Tone and U Asking Me is congested — watch for crowding and interference at the first handful of fences.

Fr Gilligansvoyge carries the best raw placed form of all the redistributed hold-up types — five from five in the recent record on Good ground — and if it finds an unimpeded run from further back than usual it is the most likely of the rear group to make a late impact.

Not So Serious is the only runner with a recent win (last time out on Good) coming into this field of largely winless recent form horses — monitor how Slevin positions it early, as moving from hold-up to a more prominent role would be a significant tactical upgrade for this shape.

races.name: Majestic Hotel Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Chasing Blues
runners_data.note: Front-runner with hurdling headgear, trained by De Bromhead, back in 22 days; recent form shows a fall and a remote eighth suggesting jumping fragility at pace — one of the three confirmed lead-setters but consistency questions make it vulnerable if the gallop gets fierce.

runners_data.name: Fortis Et Liber
runners_data.note: One hurdling run to date, placed on Good ground over 18f for Colin Bowe — lightly exposed form is intriguing in a maiden, prominent style suits a strong-pace scenario where he can travel kindly without getting involved in the front-running battle.

runners_data.name: Jack Spriggins
runners_data.note: 728-day absence is a huge red flag regardless of style; hold-up profile suits a scenario where he can organise off a hot pace, but Barry T Murphy's flat-track form history offers no confidence that this comeback will be sharp enough over an unfamiliar hurdle trip.

runners_data.name: Jury Foreman
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a tongue-tie and blinkers, but OR 94 makes him the weakest of the three pace-setters on form — most likely to be dropped early if the principals quicken, yet still contributes materially to the pace pressure from the outset.

runners_data.name: Nothintodowithme
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with tongue-tie, only one hurdles run (pulled up on Good) and 80 days off the track — completely unexposed but that sole start offers no encouragement, and a strong gallop will ask serious questions of both his jumping and stamina.

runners_data.name: O'Callaghan Can
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with multiple placed efforts at 16-24f on Good ground — no wins yet but the four placed finishes show durability, and a pace collapse scenario where he sits just behind the frontrunners and pounces late is precisely the shape his form profile suits.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Cromwell-trained prominent racer with four placed efforts from six hurdles runs, all on Good or similar; the pattern of finishing third repeatedly suggests a horse that travels into races well but lacks a final gear — a contested, stamina-testing gallop could be the leveller that finally gets him home.

runners_data.name: World As One
runners_data.note: Mullins/Hayes is the standout booking in this field, and the horse has staying form at 18-20f on Good; the confirmed front-running style carries inherent risk with two rivals pushing the pace, but class and connections give this horse the best chance of setting a manageable lead and kicking clear.

runners_data.name: Champ Young
runners_data.note: Solid trainer angle aside, this is a genuine hold-up horse — its two hurdling runs showed back-end finishing patterns — pushed into a midfield map slot because the rear is overcrowded; that positional compromise means the strong pace may generate gaps it cannot exploit from where it will actually race.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced eight-year-old with uncertain style (U) and 117 days off the track for Mark Fahey; one hurdling run placing sixth on Good is the sum total of evidence — the long absence and unknown tactical profile make assessment almost impossible, though freshness occasionally counts in weak maidens.

runners_data.name: The Orphan Girl
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in finishes and back in just 11 days after a remote ninth — hold-up profile means she needs a truly end-to-end gallop to get any chance of finishing off, but the fading tendency undermines confidence even in the most favourable stamina-test scenario.

runners_data.name: Simple Things
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid placed form at staying trips including two seconds — however, this is a horse pushed into a midfield map slot from the rear due to field congestion, so its natural finishing style will be compromised by where it actually finds itself racing; rated OR 107, the class concession to top-weighted rivals adds another layer of difficulty.

races.paceDynamic: World As One, Chasing Blues, and Jury Foreman are all confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field, and with Good ground at Tramore ensuring no attrition excuse, a strong, contested gallop from the outset is virtually certain. These three will press each other from the off, creating genuine pace pressure over 2m½f that will stretch the field and punish any horse lacking stamina or tactical nous. The race shape strongly favours horses who can settle in a prominent-to-midfield position behind the pace battle and pick off tiring leaders from the second-last hurdle — in other words, prominent types with reserves and genuine stayers will be the primary beneficiaries, not the pace-setters who burn each other out. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate cleanly — of those likely to secure their natural position up front, World As One (Mullins/Hayes) and Chasing Blues (De Bromhead) have the class and connections to actually get there, while Champ Young and Simple Things, mapped here as midfield, are true hold-up horses who are unlikely to find the clear air they need with so many horses ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominents Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out across the first mile and the race is won by a horse travelling prominently but under restraint behind them.
scenarios.body: World As One, Chasing Blues, and Jury Foreman set a fierce gallop that sees at least two of them crying enough before the final hurdle, with a horse like Seven Towers or O'Callaghan Can — who consistently post placed efforts sitting handily — sweeping past the deflated leaders. This shape most directly rewards consistent prominent types who have stamina evidence and the ability to quicken off a strong pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters — most likely World As One given Mullins/Hayes quality — is allowed to dictate at a controlled enough clip and proves strongest in the straight.
scenarios.body: Rather than an all-out burn-up, World As One uses superior class and jumping technique to dictate terms at a sustainable pace, kicking clear at the second-last before rivals can organise a challenge. Mullins' 14/47 T14 strike rate and Brian Hayes aboard make this horse the most likely of the trio to both lead and stay leading.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal and the front three completely empty out, allowing mid-to-rear types to pick their way through the carnage in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A genuine war of attrition would theoretically open the door for Simple Things or Nothintodowithme, both of whom have placed form at staying trips, to finish off tired rivals. However, Simple Things and Champ Young — the true hold-up horses — are mapped to midfield out of role and face a structural disadvantage in getting the gaps they need, limiting the realistic ceiling of this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Lands Maiden
scenarios.trigger: If the race deteriorates into a messy, slow-burning contest with late carnage at hurdles and an unexposed runner capitalises on mass attrition.
scenarios.body: Fortis Et Liber, with only one hurdles run to hand but a placed effort on identical Good ground over 18f, or the lightly-raced Hashtag Doyen, could benefit from chaos that wipes out more exposed rivals. These unknowns are capable of stepping forward in a maiden context where more established runners self-destruct on the pace.

watchPoints.text: World As One — watch whether Brian Hayes allows him to dictate alone or whether Chasing Blues and Jury Foreman push him into an unsustainable gallop; if all three go hammer and tongs from flag-fall, the race could be blown apart by the second last and the winner comes from off the pace.

Jury Foreman — rated OR 94 and wearing blinkers and tongue-tie, this confirmed front-runner is the most likely of the three pace-setters to crack under pressure; watch for him being dropped and weakening quickly, which will signal whether the pace has been genuinely brutal.

Simple Things and Champ Young — both are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield out of positional necessity; if the pace is fierce and the field strings out, they may find themselves boxed in rather than producing their natural finishing runs — watch their position at halfway.

Seven Towers — four career placed finishes without winning is a pattern worth noting; if Keith Donoghue has him travelling sweetly in second or third gear at the top of the straight, he could finally break his duck, but watch for the characteristic flattening out on the run-in.

Fortis Et Liber — only one hurdles run but placed on identical Good ground; with Ricky Doyle aboard for Colin Bowe, watch whether he travels with any fluency in the early stages — if he jumps well and settles prominently, his unexposed profile could make him dangerous at a big price.

races.name: John Fairbrother Memorial Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: Two wins on good ground and competitive form at this level, but the finish-fade flag is genuine — the hold-up style means Keith Donoghue will need a strong pace to run into, and on a day when Galileo Springs controls tempo, that may simply not materialise.

runners_data.name: Galileo Springs
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with a trainer in decent 14-day form (1/2) and a strong record on good ground (9/11 sim-going strikes); she won over 17f good last time and this 2m½f trip is within range, though the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.92 is puzzling given she IS the pace-setter here — her chance is real if she gets away cleanly.

runners_data.name: Golden Wings
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who races from hold-up, has just two placed efforts from five runs on going that resembles today's, and the P flag on recent form is a concern — Sam Ewing takes over and needs the pace to truly collapse before this one comes into it.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f on good ground and holds a decent each-way profile, but the finish-fade warning combined with a hold-up style and modest recent form (-74010) make it hard to be confident even if the pace suits; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim is a small help on the weights.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with 15 from 15 in similar-going conditions and placed in two of her last three starts at this trip; Josh Williamson's 3lb claim is useful, and the prominent style means she should be ideally positioned to pounce if Galileo Springs comes back to the field.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has won twice at Tramore over this distance on good ground and thrives in this precise context — 42 days since last run is the one query, but Carl Millar's 5lb claim offsets the penalty and the course-and-distance profile is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Like An Ocean
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with just two runs, winning on debut over 2m on good ground at Tramore; the step up to 2m½f is unexplored territory and Harry Sexton's 7lb claim flatters the allotted weight, but inexperience over this trip is a real risk.

runners_data.name: Rare Times
runners_data.note: Naturally a prominent racer whose real preference is to race forward, but with Galileo Springs, Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express, and Like An Ocean ahead of her in the queue, she is likely to find herself further back than suits; the STYLE_FIT discount and modest recent form (no wins from four runs) temper any bold assessment, though J J Slevin's booking is an upgrade.

runners_data.name: Bravewhenineedtobe
runners_data.note: Last winning run was over 2m6f on good ground under Ms Mullins' care, and she is a natural front-runner who genuinely wants to be prominent — the problem is she has not run for 717 days and will be racing out of position in this crowded pace scenario; fitness must be the primary concern before style even enters the equation.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: A true hold-up mare mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear, carrying the lowest OR (81) and consistent form figures of 5-5-5-6-9 on good ground — Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps marginally but the finish-fade flag and weak form cycle make it very hard to construct a winning scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Galileo Springs is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the front on good ground over 2m½f at Tramore. Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express, and Like An Ocean are all legitimate prominent racers who will press for positions just behind the leader, creating a compact early pack rather than a breakaway, which should keep the pace honest without turning it frantic. Del Boys Diva, Golden Wings, and Small Bucks are natural hold-up operators who will be content to settle in behind, waiting for their moment in the straight — but both Del Boys Diva and Small Bucks carry finish-fade flags that temper their claims late. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure a front-rank berth: Rare Times and Bravewhenineedtobe are genuine prominent horses redistributed to midfield because Galileo Springs, Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express, and Like An Ocean will fill those forward slots first, meaning Rare Times and Bravewhenineedtobe are likely to race out of their natural position. This shape — a single front-runner with a pressured but controlled pace — favours horses that can sit handy, travel smoothly just off the pace, and produce a sustained galloping finish, making on-pace prominent types the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Galileo Springs Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Galileo Springs is allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop unchallenged and the pace remains controlled throughout.
scenarios.body: Galileo Springs settles the race from the front on ground she handles well, and the lack of any rival willing to take her on means she can conserve energy before stretching clear from two out. Horses positioned just behind — Sea Of Doubt and Tingarran Express — are best placed to chase her home if she tires, as they travel handy without fighting for cover.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to find out Galileo Springs in the closing stages, allowing handy-travelling rivals to wear her down.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Doubt's strong record on good ground and consistent form figures around this trip make her the likeliest to pick up the pieces, while Tingarran Express's proven course-and-distance wins give her legitimate claims as a galloping finisher. Both horses sit close enough to the action to capitalise the moment Galileo Springs comes off the bridle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely strong pace that burns them all out, opening a late run for patient horses from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Golden Wings has shown the ability to close from deep when conditions suit, and Del Boys Diva — despite the finish-fade concern — has winning form on good ground and can produce a challenge if the pace collapses. The scenario is undermined slightly by Small Bucks also carrying a fade flag, narrowing the field of credible closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Rare Times and Bravewhenineedtobe causes mid-race traffic issues and the race develops chaotically, allowing a longer-shot to land the spoils.
scenarios.body: Bravewhenineedtobe, whose last winning run came over 2m6f on good ground and who is naturally suited to racing prominently, could find a clear passage if the pace fragments — though 717 days off the track is a massive query against. Rare Times, a genuinely prominent type forced wide in the pack, could also capitalise if the race falls apart, though her form figures in this class do not inspire confidence.

watchPoints.text: Tingarran Express has won twice at Tramore over this exact course and distance on good ground — if the 42-day break has not blunted her, she is the most obvious danger to Galileo Springs once they turn for home.

Bravewhenineedtobe has not run for 717 days and is naturally suited to racing prominently, but is likely to be trapped in a midfield pocket — watch for signs of greenness or sluggishness early that could confirm the layoff has taken its toll.

Like An Ocean is stepping markedly up in trip on just her second career start — if she gets lit up by the early pace and burns out before the final flight, she could bring several rivals behind her into trouble.

Sea Of Doubt's jockey Josh Williamson claims 3lb and has a 2/10 14-day record for the trainer — monitor in the market for any significant move that would suggest connections are confident she handles the slight dip in trip from her last two runs.

Rare Times and Bravewhenineedtobe are both trained by Ms Margaret Mullins and will likely be competing for the same mid-pack space — watch how each is ridden from the gate, as the one that manages to get forward early could be significantly advantaged over the one forced to cover extra ground.

races.name: Walsh Butler Electrical Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Banphrionsa Alainn
runners_data.note: Trainer Leahy 0/3 in the 14-day window; placed twice in similar Good-ground hurdles but finishes weakly, and while shown in midfield, her natural instinct is to sit deeply off the pace — that hold-up style is a significant liability in this slow-tempo shape.|

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Modest form string (9P-9U7) on a mix of Good and Soft, no wins or places, and a genuine closer by nature who will struggle badly if the compressed midfield means she cannot find daylight in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Hello Below
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and key pace-setter; Good-ground form is solid (two runs, both in Good), and with no rival likely to challenge early, she controls the race entirely from the front — the race revolves around whether she can sustain that lead.|

runners_data.name: Hunskelper
runners_data.note: Absent 90 days, trainer Collins returns 1/14 in the 14-day window, and this is a hold-up horse by inclination who has been pushed into a midfield slot purely by the weight of closers in the field — the layoff and positional compromise are both negatives.|

runners_data.name: Mila Ballerina
runners_data.note: Visor fitted, jockey Charlie O'Dwyer (3lb claimer) aboard for trainer Conor O'Dwyer — best effort a 5th over 2m2f on Good, and as a hold-up horse she needs the pace to quicken ahead of her, which is unlikely in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Nancy Wheeler
runners_data.note: Three runs, three zeros, all on Good ground and all at shorter trips; trainer Curling 0/7 in the 14-day window and this horse routinely settles in the rear with no notable late kick.|

runners_data.name: Queenofqueenstreet
runners_data.note: Two runs, finished 12th and 15th on Good ground at Tramore — a consistent backmarker with nothing in her form to suggest she can overcome the positional disadvantage of sitting deeply in a slowly-run race.|

runners_data.name: Quiet In Bresil
runners_data.note: Six runs on Good, returning after 77 days; her 5th at 2m (16f) is the best run in the book but she is a hold-up specialist who genuinely needs strong pace — which this race will almost certainly not provide.|

runners_data.name: Road To The Sea
runners_data.note: Fell last time out, shaped as a backmarker across five runs; the trainer 0/4 in the 14-day window and the combination of a fall, a modest form line and a natural rear-sitting style makes this a tough ask.|

runners_data.name: Room For One More
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained, 4 days since last run, and finished 9th in a Good-ground maiden hurdle last time — she has the yard's firepower behind her and if she can park prominently, the recency and stable form makes her a prime candidate to stalk Hello Below.|

runners_data.name: Treacys Ella
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (two runs, 5th and 8th on Good), style genuinely unknown — that uncertainty is a small positive as she may naturally race more prominently than her stablemates; trainer Queally 4/10 in the 14-day window is a notable angle.|

runners_data.name: Gratitudeforgrace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained 4-year-old, 4/42 for the yard in the window, but genuinely holds up by nature — placed in midfield on the map only because the field is saturated with closers, so her chance depends on more pace materialising than Hello Below alone provides.|

runners_data.name: I'm Gold
runners_data.note: Tongue tie, finishing 14th and 13th across two Good-ground runs; a true rear-of-field operator who lacks the natural positioning to exploit a slowly-run race, and the form figures offer little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Kenny's Jewel
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin in the saddle — stable upgrade in jockey quality — and the 6th at Navan (2m1f, Good) is the most competitive run in this field; headgear previously fitted and the hold-up style is a concern, but Slevin's ability to organise a horse may help.|

runners_data.name: Thedreamistilalive
runners_data.note: Tongue tie, two runs both on Good and both mid-pack finishes (9th, 15th); a 13-day turnaround and a claimer in the saddle — nothing in the profile to suggest she can produce better than a modest finish from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Lady Aquarelle
runners_data.note: Five runs, best finish a 7th over 2m6f on Soft; tongue tie and breast girth fitted, placed pulled up last time — her stronger runs have come on softer ground and the Good surface here compounds the concern.|

races.paceDynamic: Hello Below is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner mares maiden hurdle over 2m5f at Tramore on Good ground, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, she will set a measured, uncontested gallop from the front. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up and midfield types — Banphrionsa Alainn, Hunskelper, I'm Gold, Gratitudeforgrace, Kenny's Jewel, Road To The Sea, Quiet In Bresil, Fervida and Lady Aquarelle are all genuine closers compressed into midfield on the map because there are far more hold-up horses in this race than the shape can naturally accommodate at the rear. With Hello Below dictating a comfortable, unforced tempo, the danger is that she lopes into the straight with energy in reserve and the chasing pack — largely comprised of horses unable to get their preferred wide-margin hold-up position — arrives collectively rather than individually. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape heavily favours front-running or prominent racing profiles, and any horse capable of travelling close to Hello Below without exertion will enjoy a decisive positional advantage over the genuine closers stuck in a congested midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hello Below Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Below bowls along in front at a comfortable clip and meets every hurdle cleanly, she controls the race throughout.
scenarios.body: With no pressure from behind and a steady Good-ground gallop, she arrives at the last with petrol remaining and simply outstays rivals who have had to do more work from further back. This shape strongly benefits the horse able to dictate and quicken from the front over 2m5f at Tramore.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or midfield runner tracks Hello Below closely from the outset and produces a clean challenge from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Room For One More, trained by Mullins and fresh from a recent run, or Treacys Ella — both capable of racing handily — could stalk the pace and produce a decisive late effort when Hello Below ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Below sets an unexpectedly strong early gallop that burns off prominent horses and leaves the race open for late finishers.
scenarios.body: A genuinely fast pace would compress finishing times and allow a true hold-up horse to rattle home on the outer, though this is unlikely given Hello Below's confirmed front-running style is measured rather than suicidal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart; Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, loose horses or jumping errors disrupt the field and the race is run at an uneven, disjointed tempo.
scenarios.body: Carnage mid-race in a 16-runner maiden hurdle can randomise the result entirely, promoting whoever survives the incident cleanest regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: Hello Below — monitor her jump at the first three hurdles; any early mistake under Ricky Doyle could immediately cede the lead she is guaranteed to inherit uncontested, reshaping the entire race.|

Room For One More — watch whether Brian Hayes elects to park prominently or settles into a midfield queue; a Mullins horse running just four days after its last start is worth following from the off.|

Kenny's Jewel — JJ Slevin may attempt to push for a closer position than this horse's natural style suggests; if he gets her into the first four, her chance improves materially over the hold-up scenario.|

Gratitudeforgrace — despite Elliott's numbers, her redistribution from the rear to midfield is an artificial map position; if she does naturally travel closer to the pace than her form suggests, the Elliott/Ewing combination becomes live.|

Watch for crowding and interference at the early hurdles with 16 runners — a compressed midfield of hold-up types will cause bunching, and any horse caught behind fallers or unseated riders between hurdle one and three could lose considerable ground.|

races.name: Comeragh Veterinary Kilmackthomas Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Won last time on good ground over 22f and carries cheekpieces; a genuine hold-up horse trained by Declan Queally, ridden by his son Mr D L Queally, who will need Latopix to come back to him in the final stages — similar-going form reads 1W2P from six runs, suggesting the conditions suit.|

runners_data.name: Ryan's Son
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and has a pattern of folding late in his form string, which is a concern over this extended 2m5f on good; a true hold-up type who would need an unusually sharp collapse in pace to win, and the 35-day break adds a small query.|

runners_data.name: Jacko Star
runners_data.note: 191 days off the track is a substantial absence and Keith Donoghue inherits a horse with a string of fourth-place finishes on similar ground; stays well enough at this trip but has never won on good, and the layoff makes it hard to take a short price.|

runners_data.name: Latopix
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner, proven on good ground with two placed efforts over 20-22f and Henry De Bromhead's team in strong recent form (T14: 4/34); no rival is likely to pressure him early, and O'Keeffe can nurse him into the straight — the key question is whether he has enough to hold on.|

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with an outstanding record on good ground (sim-going: 15/15, 2W6P) and ran just 12 days ago so is racecourse fit; wears a hood and naturally prominent, giving him the best position behind Latopix — if the leader fades, he is first to benefit.|

runners_data.name: Good World
runners_data.note: Solid course winner on heavy ground and an 11-year-old veteran with tactical nous; at heart a true hold-up type pushed into the midfield map here because the field is backmarker-heavy, meaning Michael Kenneally (5) may not find the clean run late that this horse truly needs — STYLE_FIT 0.93 tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 22f last time and has a course placing — the best form profile among the closers; Josh Williamson (3) takes a 3lb claim and if the pace quickens in the straight, Tolka Row's recent winning run and strong similar-going figures (5/5, 1W2P) make him the most credible challenger from the hold-up group.|

runners_data.name: Boston Beach
runners_data.note: Trained by Gordon Elliott but carrying a fade-in-finish flag and a string of low finishes recently; a natural hold-up type shifted into midfield by the overcrowded rear, and Danny Gilligan faces a tactical puzzle — STYLE_FIT 0.92 and no win on good ground in recent form mean expectations should be modest.|

runners_data.name: Hillstar Blues
runners_data.note: Five-year-old lightly raced on good, with a fade flag and 92 days between runs; Anna McGuinness (7) takes a 7lb claim that helps the weight, but the horse's best form came on soft and the style redistribution into midfield further reduces the probability of a bold show.|

runners_data.name: Diamond Secret
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has been consistently mid-table in form over shorter trips, stepping up to 2m5f here; a true backmarker type mapped into midfield given the field's composition, and Niall Moore (5) will need things to go perfectly for a first win — STYLE_FIT 0.90 leaves little room for optimism.|

runners_data.name: Moonlight Paradise
runners_data.note: Also hooded and another Paul Nolan five-year-old still searching for a win; best finish on good ground was fifth, and a P in recent form raises a jumping reliability query — Eoin Staples (5) faces a tough task getting this out-of-role hold-up horse into a position to influence the race.|

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at four, with no wins and a recent P in the form string suggesting jumping issues at speed; the true backmarker profile is squeezed into midfield, Daniel King will struggle to find a clean run, and the soft ground bias in form figures (4/15 on good) is a notable negative.|

races.paceDynamic: Latopix is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m5f trip on good ground at Tramore. Tullyveery Lad is the one prominent horse who could push forward and at least sit in Latopix's slipstream, giving the front end some shape, but neither horse is likely to turn this into a war. The rest of the field — including Mighty Berkshire, Ryan's Son, Tolka Row and Jacko Star — are genuine hold-up types who will need the pace to collapse late, and with Good World, Boston Beach, Hillstar Blues, Diamond Secret, Moonlight Paradise and Ray Gun all true hold-up horses compressed into mid-division due to the overcrowded rear, the field holds far more backmarkers than the race shape can accommodate; Latopix and Tullyveery Lad are overwhelmingly most likely to secure their natural positions. A controlled, uncontested lead on good ground over an extended trip strongly favours prominent types who can travel smoothly into the straight without burning reserves, with Latopix ideally placed to dictate and Tullyveery Lad best positioned to pounce if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Latopix Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Latopix secures the lead unchallenged and O'Keeffe sets a measured, race-long gallop that saps the closers.
scenarios.body: Latopix has proven front-running ability and two recent second-place finishes on good ground at this sort of trip, and a solo lead at a sensible tempo on a fair-sized Tramore circuit allows him to preserve enough in the tank to repel any challenger; Tullyveery Lad, sitting prominent throughout, is ideally placed to pick up the pieces if the leader tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and the leaders come back to the closers in the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Tolka Row, a course-record winner over 2m2f on good ground, and Mighty Berkshire, who struck on good ground last time, are the most credible closers with the form and profile to benefit from a late drop in tempo; the good ground ensures the surface does not blunt their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Poaches Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely soft and a prominent racer travels into contention cheaply before the field wakes up.
scenarios.body: Tullyveery Lad is the beneficiary here, with an excellent record over 24f+ on good ground and a recent run just 12 days ago keeping him spot-sharp; if Latopix stutters at a hurdle or gets into a rhythm that invites Tullyveery Lad to pass, the latter's proven course-and-distance profile makes him dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded rear somehow clears and a true hold-up type — Good World, Boston Beach or Hillstar Blues — finds unobstructed racing room.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally undermined because these horses are racing out of their natural role, squeezed into midfield rather than the rear they prefer, reducing the likelihood of a clean finishing run; Good World, the most experienced of the group with a course win on heavy and proven staying form, is the best-placed if this unlikely shape materialises.

watchPoints.text: Tullyveery Lad is only 12 days off his last run, travels prominent naturally behind Latopix, and his 15-run similar-going record (2W6P) makes him the most dangerous horse if Latopix fades from the second-last hurdle.|

Latopix is the sole front-runner and if O'Keeffe misjudges the pace and goes too slow, the closers grouped in mid-division — particularly Tolka Row and Mighty Berkshire — will have enough energy to reel him in over the final two flights.|

Ryan's Son is flagged for fading in the finish and has regressed over longer trips recently; if the betting market shortens him based on his OR, Eoghan Finegan (5) should be watched to see whether he settles better here than his recent form suggests.|

The cluster of six redistributed hold-up types (Good World, Boston Beach, Hillstar Blues, Diamond Secret, Moonlight Paradise, Ray Gun) will be competing for the same ground from three out — watch for traffic problems and interference in the straight as they try to find gaps simultaneously.|

Jacko Star's 191-day absence is the longest gap in the field; watch how Keith Donoghue positions him early — if the horse travels well in the first mile it would be a positive signal, but his historical finishing positions suggest he rarely improves from a point-to-point of form over this sort of distance.|

races.name: Clem Jacob Hire Flat Race

runners_data.name: Cloneen To The Max
runners_data.note: Trainer Don Browne has had no winners from 2 runners in the past 14 days; a confirmed hold-up horse with a fade pattern in finishes and four recent top-10 finishes on good, though 0 wins or places from 5 similar-going runs — the redistribution into midfield means it races forward of its natural comfort zone, and that positional compromise tempers its prospects.|

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lad
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with a completely unknown running style; Mr H C Swan takes the ride for Alan McIntyre (0 from 3 in 14 days) and with no form string available the horse is an information vacuum — anything is possible but evidence is thin.|

runners_data.name: Tale Of Intrigue
runners_data.note: Mr T A Halford (7lb claimer) rides for D Buckley (0 from 2 in 14 days); a genuine hold-up horse with a solid recent run of 3rd, 4th, and 5th on good ground, giving 1 place from 5 similar-going runs — best served if the field bunches and a clear run materialises in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Call My Name
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old trained by Andrew Slattery (3 from 31 in 14 days — the standout trainer strike rate in the field); unknown style and no form string, but the Slattery yard is firing and the 5lb claimer Mr A P Ryan takes the ride, making this one of the more interesting unknown quantities.|

runners_data.name: Charles Kickham
runners_data.note: Flat headgear noted; a hold-up horse by profile whose three runs (8th, 4th, 6th) have all come in similar distances and two on good — the best of those finishes was a 4th on good, and racing here in a slot that is further forward than natural adds a layer of risk to an already modest recent form profile.|

runners_data.name: Mountain Sky
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, trained by Gerard O'Leary (1 from 15 in 14 days) and ridden by Mr J L Gleeson; two consecutive second-place finishes on good ground and two runs at this trip or shorter suggest the step up in trip is workable — uncontested lead on this track is a significant tactical advantage.|

runners_data.name: Long'way
runners_data.note: Trained by W P Mullins with 14 winners from 47 runners in the past 14 days — the dominant trainer in the field by volume; Mr P W Mullins takes the ride and the horse debuts with an unknown style, but the powerful Mullins operation at full tilt makes Long'way one to consider irrespective of the pace shape.|

runners_data.name: No Pass Port
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon (0 from 21 in 14 days) sends out this four-year-old who finished 9th on good ground last time over 17f; a hold-up profile with a fade flag and the lightest weight in the field at 158lbs — only one run to assess and it did not encourage.

races.paceDynamic: Mountain Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressurise them, Mr J L Gleeson can dictate terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m½f on good ground at Tramore. The remainder of the field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Cloneen To The Max, Tale Of Intrigue, Charles Kickham, and No Pass Port all want to come from off the pace — meaning the race will almost certainly develop into a single file procession behind Mountain Sky before the field fans out entering the straight. The field carries more genuine hold-up horses than the pace map can place at the rear, with Cloneen To The Max and Charles Kickham redistributed into midfield slots they will not naturally occupy, and both carry a style-fit discount as a result. This shape strongly favours Mountain Sky and any horse comfortable racing prominently in second or third, as an uncontested, economical leader sets an even gallop that is unlikely to be quick enough to string the field out, leaving finishing speed from just off the pace as the decisive quality.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mountain Sky Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mountain Sky is allowed to lead uncontested and sets an honest but comfortable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Mountain Sky bowls along in front without a rival willing or able to go with them, conserving energy through the final bend before the pilot asks for a kick in the straight; the absence of pace pressure means the race is run to suit a horse that has raced to front prominently in all three career starts and who already has two second-place finishes on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Mountain Sky in second or third wheels out smoothly in the straight and outstays the leader.
scenarios.body: With the pace gentle, the gap between the leader and the second horse stays compact throughout, and a prominent tracker who travels sweetly can sprint past a fading Mountain Sky in the final furlong; Long'way and the unknown quantities Call My Name and Moonhall Lad, if forward-going, are best placed to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Runs Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slow enough to bunch the field and a true hold-up horse finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: A compressed field at a slow tempo can allow late-closers to make ground rapidly in the home straight, but Cloneen To The Max and Charles Kickham — the most likely beneficiaries — are racing out of their natural rear position and carry meaningful style-fit discounts, reducing confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mountain Sky is headed or fades abruptly and the race becomes a scramble from the home turn.
scenarios.body: An unexpected pace collapse opens the race up for any horse travelling kindly mid-pack, but the sheer dominance of hold-up types in the field means no natural prominent racer is on hand to capitalise cleanly, making this a chaotic and low-probability scenario.

watchPoints.text: Mountain Sky's jockey Mr J L Gleeson — watch whether they attempt to steal a march from the gate or deliberately settle; if Mountain Sky is gifted a soft lead with no company, the advantage could prove decisive in a field so heavily weighted towards rear-runners.

Long'way (W P Mullins / Mr P W Mullins) debuts as a complete unknown — watch market moves closely before the off, as the Mullins yard's 14-from-47 strike rate in the past fortnight means any significant support here should be taken seriously regardless of the absence of a form string.

Cloneen To The Max and Charles Kickham — both true hold-up horses placed into midfield on the pace map due to overcrowding at the rear; watch whether either can actually secure their natural position or whether they are forced even further forward and out of their comfort zone entirely.

Call My Name — Andrew Slattery's 3-from-31 runner count in 14 days is the best conversion rate among the trainers represented here; with a 5lb claimer up and no form to frame expectations, any notable drifting or shortening in the market warrants close attention.
